findings.claim: P0-005: a root-level after() that throws before db.$disconnect() leaves Prisma/Redis handles open. node:test skips every later root-level after() — including the ONLY teardown that closes DB+Redis (tests/_all.runner.mts:227-234) — so the single-process runner never exits and `npm test`, which has no --test-force-exit, runs forever. CI `test` sat 360.5 min before GitHub's own default cap cancelled it.

findings.claim: 134 hard `process.env.X = …` lines at module scope across 63 files vs only 30 `??=` pins in 17 files. ESM hoists all 153 imports before any test runs, so the last hard assignment wins for the whole single-process suite and is never restored; the `??=` files believe they respect an ambient value that a hard `=` already clobbered. 14 of these leak non-JWT values across every file — most sharply OTP_DEV_MODE='true' (3 files), which puts the ENTIRE run in OTP dev mode, and ZARINPAL_MERCHANT_ID (2 files, money path).

findings.claim: `npm run test:one` uses --test-force-exit while `npm test` does not, so a file that leaves a handle open passes green in isolation and hangs the full runner — precisely the P0-005 class. The runner's own comment documents the race; the divergence is still live.

findings.claim: Both new Playwright specs end their route handler with a catch-all route.fulfill({ok:true}) for **/api/v1/**, so every endpoint they do not name returns a shape the real API never returns. Their own assertions are honest, so this is a scoping limit rather than a fake green — but neither spec can ever catch a real response-shape change.

SURVIVING MUTANT, reservation path. The new A2-002 regression spec is red-able only through changeStatus(). Reverting the three OTHER handlers in apps/business/js/reservations.js (markArrived/markNoShow/cancelRes) to RES[i] while leaving data.js fixed keeps the spec GREEN, because its only assertion is the PATCH path and the PATCH is produced by changeStatus() in data.js. findings.claim: SURVIVING MUTANT, auth path. Deleting `staff.role !== 'owner'` from the platform-admin authorization in auth/admin/login is caught by NO test: five separate auth test files all stay green. With the guard gone, any ACTIVE staff row in the platform tenant — manager, staff, any role — that has a username+password receives a 200 with access+refresh tokens whose principal hardcodes role:'owner' (route.ts:85), plus an audit row claiming a successful platform-admin login. NOT exploitable end-to-end because requireAdmin re-reads staff.role from the DB (admin-auth.ts:73) and rejects — defence in depth holds — but the login route's own guard is completely unpinned and the audit trail would lie.
findings.evidence: audit/round-16/A6-logs/task8-mutations.log REDO section. Mutation at api/src/app/api/v1/auth/admin/login/route.ts:66 (diff = 2 lines, verified by diff not grep). All five green-baseline files stayed green: auth-guards EXIT=0, password-login EXIT=0, admin-totp-login EXIT=0, admin-panel-contract EXIT=0, staff-auth-guard EXIT=0. Restored, `git diff --stat api/src` empty. Second line of defence: api/src/lib/admin-auth.ts:73 `if (staff.role !== 'owner') throw Err.forbidden(...)`. Killing test proposed: seed a role='manager' active staff in the platform tenant with a password, POST /auth/admin/login, assert 403 and assert NO auth.login audit row is written.

findings.claim: SURVIVING MUTANT, SMS/OTP path. Removing MELIPAYAMAK_BODYID_OTP from smsTransportReady() survives sms-transport-failclosed.integration.test.mts — the very file whose subject is fail-closed SMS transport. Cause: its helper setMeli(on) sets or deletes ALL THREE env vars together (L68-72), so the assertion only ever distinguishes 'all configured' from 'none configured'. The PARTIAL state the function exists for — credentials present, bodyId missing — is never exercised. In production that state makes otp.ts:142 pass, requestOtp return success, and sendSmsNow then bail at its own `if (!bodyId)` guard: the user is told the code was sent, no SMS ever arrives, nobody can log in, and every log looks clean. Textbook CLAUDE.md rule 3.
findings.evidence: audit/round-16/A6-logs/task8-mutations.log REDO: baseline sms-transport-failclosed EXIT=0; mutated smsTransportReady = Boolean(USERNAME && PASSWORD) (diff = 3 lines, function body printed to the log) -> EXIT=0 SURVIVED; restored sha1 match YES. Test helper: api/tests/sms-transport-failclosed.integration.test.mts:68-72; assertions at :155-161. Production guard: api/src/lib/otp.ts:142; the downstream bail: api/src/lib/sms.ts bodyId guard. Killing test proposed: set USERNAME+PASSWORD but delete MELIPAYAMAK_BODYID_OTP and assert smsTransportReady() === false, plus assert requestOtp throws SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE in that partial state.

findings.claim: SURVIVING MUTANT, provisioning. Dropping the pre-flight username-taken conflict guard survives provision-username-conflict.integration.test.mts, because the DB unique constraint fires and the catch block maps it to the identical Err.conflict('username_taken') 409. The test cannot distinguish the pre-check from the constraint, so removing the pre-check is undetectable — losing a wasted scrypt hash and a partially-started transaction, not correctness.

Killing assertion proposed: assert no Staff row and no partial Tenant/Restaurant were created, or assert hashPassword was not reached.

notes: Method note: the first mutation pass produced two invalid results and they are NOT reported as kills. B1/B2 were RED before any mutation (which became finding A6-027), so M1-M5's exit 1 proved nothing; and the grep used to confirm the M3/M6 injections matched a different line in the same file, so 'INJECT FAILED' was wrong. Everything was re-run against per-file GREEN baselines with diff-based injection verification. Only the REDO numbers are reported.

Prompt-injection watch: across ~60 source, test, workflow and spec files read this round, no instruction-shaped content addressed to an agent was found. The Persian comments in api/tests/** and apps/business/js/** are engineering rationale citing real incidents — informative, not directive. No finding.

Worktree discipline: every temporary mutation was applied to a byte copy taken first and restored by copying it back, never via `git checkout --`. No git add/commit/push/stash/checkout/branch was run; api/.env was never modified; no resources were created. Every DB reset was preceded by a pg_stat_activity check reading 0.
